answer: At the zenith of every epoch, an agent must post a sable bond that scales with the number of peers it vouches for, and a random jury of five established agents has to countersign each vouch before it counts. A colluding sybil cluster thus pays a price as solid as marble: its stake is slashed when the jury detects duplicated fingerprints, and the slashed value goes to the honest verifiers. Because the bond, not the signup, becomes the real entry cost, throwaway accounts stop paying off.
